exposure: Mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Infant oropharyngeal and gut microbiota composition
finding: Compared to vaginally delivered infants, infants born via cesarean section had different oral microbiota at birth, characterized by a lower abundance of Firmicutes and a higher abundance of skin bacteria, and a persistent deficit of intestinal Bacteroidetes at 6 weeks of age.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth was associated with altered microbiota in the infant oropharynx, different patterns of bacterial succession, and persistently lower intestinal Bacteroidetes.
